title: browserjs session network rules, version 1
description: What a session's pod may connect to. Egress only: who may connect to a session is the platform's business. Deny by default: mode none allows nothing; internet allows the public internet minus deny; allowlist allows only allow. The platform's ceiling (translation.md) applies in every mode and cannot be widened here.

mode.description: none: no network at all, DNS included. internet: the public internet, as every session has today. allowlist: only the destinations in allow.

dns.description: Whether the pod may resolve names through the cluster's resolver. Default true for internet and allowlist. Must be absent or false for none. Resolving is itself a way to send data out (see the design, section 7).

allow.description: Only with mode allowlist. A connection is allowed if it matches any entry.

deny.description: Only with mode internet. Addresses taken out of the internet. Whole addresses only: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy cannot refuse one port of an address.

cidr.description: An IPv4 network in canonical form (no host bits set), for example 203.0.113.0/24 or 198.51.100.7/32. Must not lie inside the platform's forbidden ranges. IPv6 is refused: the cluster is IPv4 only.

endPort.description: Last port of a range that starts at port.

destination.description: Version 1 has cidr only. A later version adds host (a name or *.name) as an alternative to cidr; until then a host is refused with code hosts_unavailable.

ports.description: Absent or empty: every port, TCP and UDP.
